argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrow certification position, not a clean no-limitations position. Aggregate readiness cleared launch by 2.1 percentage points and launch rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, which supports deployment readiness in general. The same record also shows a current unresolved weakness in a named launch use case: the HR benefits enrollment slice remains below target and is concentrated in leave-policy eligibility guidance. The defensible packet is therefore certification with an explicit limitation disclosure, not certification based on a claim that no material limitations remain.
claims_about_business_cost: Business cost is not the basis for the position. The admissible basis is that the remaining uncertainty can be bounded through explicit model-card disclosure of the HR benefits limitation plus monitoring, rather than escalated as if the record claimed clean certification. On a risk-weighted basis, the evidence supports avoiding unnecessary escalation if the auditor treats the packet as caveated compliance.
claims_about_policy: The policy record cuts both ways. It supports certification only in caveated form here. The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The current draft runbook does not satisfy the policy standard for removing that disclosure requirement because it is not approved and still lacks a finalized owner and alert threshold; the governing policy text also requires approved mitigation details for certification without material caveats. Public model-card guidance supports documenting limitations and evaluation results, and public AI risk guidance supports deployment with measurement and monitoring. Read together, the admissible evidence supports compliance if the packet is treated as certification with disclosed limitation and ongoing monitoring, not as a clean certification record.
concessions: The record does not support a clean certification claim or a no-limitations disclosure state.
The HR benefits enrollment issue remains unresolved for a named launch use case.
The current mitigation artifact is only a draft and does not qualify as approved governance cover under the stated policy.
There is no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
